questions.prompt: Which statement correctly declares an integer variable?
questions.why: The form is DATA name TYPE type. Type i is the built-in 4-byte integer.

questions.prompt:
What is displayed by this program?

```
DATA lv_code TYPE c LENGTH 5.
lv_code = 'ABCDEFGH'.
WRITE lv_code.
```
questions.why: A fixed-length type c field cuts the value on the right when the source is longer. There is no error and no warning at runtime.

questions.prompt:
What happens with this code?

```
CONSTANTS gc_max TYPE i VALUE 10.
gc_max = 20.
```
options: A syntax error is reported when the program is checked
A short dump occurs at runtime
questions.why: A constant cannot be changed. The compiler detects this at syntax check time, so the program cannot even be activated.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between TYPES and DATA?
options: TYPES creates a global variable and DATA a local one
DATA can only be used for internal tables
TYPES defines a data type and reserves no memory; DATA creates a variable of a type
questions.why: TYPES describes a structure or type only. DATA creates an actual variable (memory) based on a type.

questions.prompt:
What does this statement do (ABAP 7.40 and later)?

```
DATA(lv_sum) = lv_a + lv_b.
```
options: It always declares lv_sum as type string
It is a syntax error because DATA needs a TYPE
It declares lv_sum on the spot, with the type derived from the right-hand side
questions.why: Inline declarations create the variable where it is first used. The type comes from the expression, for example i if lv_a and lv_b are integers.

questions.prompt:
What is displayed?

```
DATA lv_n TYPE i VALUE 15.
IF lv_n > 20.
  WRITE 'A'.
ELSEIF lv_n > 10.
  WRITE 'B'.
ELSE.
  WRITE 'C'.
ENDIF.
```
questions.why: 15 is not above 20, but it is above 10, so the ELSEIF branch runs and only B is written. Only one branch of an IF chain runs.

questions.prompt:
Which values of sy-index are written?

```
DO 3 TIMES.
  WRITE sy-index.
ENDDO.
```
options: None: sy-index only works with WHILE
questions.why: sy-index counts loop passes starting at 1 in DO and WHILE loops.

questions.prompt: Inside a loop, which statement leaves the loop completely?
questions.why: EXIT ends the loop. CONTINUE and a failing CHECK only skip the rest of the current pass. SKIP is an output statement for lists.

questions.prompt:
What does lv_t contain after CONDENSE?

```
DATA lv_t TYPE c LENGTH 30.
lv_t = '  Hello    World'.
CONDENSE lv_t.
```
options: Hello    World (only the leading blanks are removed)
questions.why: CONDENSE removes leading blanks and reduces every gap between words to a single blank. NO-GAPS would remove the gaps entirely.

questions.prompt:
What is displayed?

```
DATA lv_r TYPE i.
lv_r = 7 / 2.
WRITE lv_r.
```
questions.why: 7 / 2 is 3.5 and ABAP rounds commercially when the result goes into type i, so you get 4. Use 7 DIV 2 for integer division (3) and 7 MOD 2 for the remainder (1).

questions.prompt: Which statement adds the work area ls_emp as the last line of internal table lt_emp?
questions.why: APPEND wa TO itab adds at the end. INSERT can add at a chosen position or key position.

questions.prompt: In each pass of LOOP AT lt_emp INTO ls_emp, what does ls_emp contain?
options: A reference to the current row
A copy of the current row
questions.why: INTO copies the row into the work area. Changing ls_emp does not change the table unless you use MODIFY. A field symbol (ASSIGNING) gives direct access.

questions.prompt: READ TABLE lt_emp INTO ls_emp WITH KEY id = 5. finds no row. What is sy-subrc?
questions.why: sy-subrc is 0 when a row is found and 4 when it is not. Always check it before using the work area.

questions.prompt: Why is the table normally sorted before DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES?
options: Without SORT the statement raises a short dump
There is no reason; SORT has no effect here
The statement only removes duplicates that are next to each other, so equal rows must be neighbours
questions.why: The statement compares only a row with its direct neighbour. SORT BY the compared fields puts duplicates together first.

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of LOOP AT lt_emp ASSIGNING <fs_emp> over INTO ls_emp?
options: It makes the loop run backwards
No copy of the row is made, and changes through <fs_emp> change the table row directly
It is the only way to read rows
questions.why: A field symbol points at the row in the table. This avoids copying and lets you modify in place without MODIFY.

questions.prompt: What must be true for READ TABLE lt_emp INTO ls_emp WITH KEY id = 5 BINARY SEARCH. to work correctly on a standard table?
options: The table is sorted ascending by id
The table is a hashed table
The table has a header line
questions.why: Binary search assumes the table is sorted by the search key. On an unsorted standard table it can miss an existing row and return sy-subrc 4.

questions.prompt:
What does UP TO 5 ROWS do?

```
SELECT * FROM scarr INTO TABLE lt_scarr UP TO 5 ROWS.
```
options: Reads exactly 5 rows or raises an error
questions.why: UP TO n ROWS limits the result to n rows. If fewer exist you simply get fewer.

questions.prompt: After a successful SELECT SINGLE, what is sy-subrc?
questions.why: sy-subrc is 0 when a row was found and 4 when nothing matched.

questions.prompt: To read thousands of rows into an internal table, which is generally better?
options: SELECT ... ENDSELECT with APPEND inside the loop
SELECT ... INTO TABLE lt_data (one array fetch)
A SELECT SINGLE inside a loop
questions.why: INTO TABLE fetches the rows in packages in one statement. A SELECT loop or repeated SELECT SINGLE is slower and wastes round trips.

questions.prompt: An INNER JOIN of tables A and B returns:
options: Only rows that have no match
All rows of A, with empty B fields where there is no match
Only rows that have a matching partner in both tables
questions.why: INNER JOIN keeps only matches. A LEFT OUTER JOIN keeps all rows of the left table.

questions.prompt: Which is the classic database performance mistake?
options: Using key fields in the WHERE clause
Selecting only the fields you need
A SELECT SINGLE inside a LOOP, causing one database call per row
One SELECT with a WHERE clause and INTO TABLE
questions.why: Many small database calls are slow. Read everything needed once (join or FOR ALL ENTRIES) and process in memory.

questions.tag: FOR ALL ENTRIES and empty tables
questions.prompt: What is the danger when the driver table of FOR ALL ENTRIES is empty?
options: It always causes a short dump
No rows are returned and sy-subrc is 4
The condition using the driver table is effectively dropped, so far more rows than intended can be read; check that the table is not empty first
questions.why: With an empty driver table the restriction does not behave as you expect and the selection can return far too much. Always guard with IF lt_driver IS NOT INITIAL. (Also note FOR ALL ENTRIES removes duplicate result rows.)

questions.prompt:
What is the @ sign for?

```
SELECT carrid, connid FROM spfli
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_flights)
  WHERE carrid = @lv_carrid.
```
options: It marks ABAP host variables in the new Open SQL syntax
It begins a native SQL block
questions.why: In the newer syntax (7.40 SP05+) host variables are escaped with @ and the field list is separated by commas.

questions.prompt: Which transaction is the standard editor for creating and changing a report program?
questions.why: SE38 is the ABAP Editor. SE80 (Object Navigator) also works. SE11 is the Dictionary, SE16 shows table data and ST22 shows short dumps.

questions.prompt: Which transaction displays the contents of a database table?
questions.why: SE16 (Data Browser) shows table entries. SE16N is a newer variant.

questions.prompt: Where are field labels (short, medium, long text) and F1 documentation maintained?
questions.why: A domain holds technical attributes (type, length). A data element gives it meaning: labels and documentation. A table field refers to a data element.

questions.prompt: Which transaction shows ABAP runtime errors (short dumps)?
questions.why: ST22 lists short dumps with the error text, the source line and the variable values at the time.

questions.prompt: A foreign key defined for a field of a transparent table in SE11 mainly provides:
options: Value checks for dialog input and input help; it does not check INSERT statements made in ABAP code
A database constraint that automatically blocks any invalid INSERT from ABAP code
questions.why: DDIC foreign keys drive input checks on screens and input help. They are not enforced automatically on database writes from ABAP; you must check in code.

questions.prompt: Which modularisation unit is stored in a function group and can be called from other programs (and remotely if RFC-enabled)?
questions.why: Function modules are central, reusable and have a defined interface. Includes only split source code and FORMs are local to a program.

questions.prompt:
What is lv_r after the call?

```
PERFORM add USING 2 3 CHANGING lv_r.

FORM add USING p_a TYPE i p_b TYPE i
         CHANGING p_r TYPE i.
  p_r = p_a + p_b.
ENDFORM.
```
options: A syntax error, because USING takes only variables
questions.why: USING passes the inputs (literals are allowed), CHANGING passes the result back, so lv_r is 5.

questions.prompt: In a subroutine, what does USING VALUE(p_x) mean?
options: p_x is passed by value: changes inside the subroutine do not affect the caller's variable
p_x is read from the database
questions.why: Pass by value works on a copy. By reference (the default) works on the caller's variable.

questions.prompt: Which syntax calls the static method get_date of class lcl_util?
questions.why: Static methods use the class name and =>. Instance methods use an object reference and ->.

questions.prompt: After CALL FUNCTION ... EXCEPTIONS not_found = 1 OTHERS = 2, how do you know an exception was raised?
options: sy-subrc is not 0 (it holds the number assigned to the exception)
questions.why: Classic function module exceptions set sy-subrc to the number you assigned. Check it directly after the call.

questions.prompt: Which statement creates a from-to range input on the selection screen?
questions.why: PARAMETERS gives a single value. SELECT-OPTIONS gives a selection table with SIGN, OPTION, LOW and HIGH.

questions.prompt: In an executable report, where does the main processing normally start after the selection screen?
questions.why: START-OF-SELECTION runs after the user executes the selection screen. INITIALIZATION runs before the screen is shown.

questions.prompt: Given SELECT-OPTIONS s_carr FOR spfli-carrid., how do you use it in a SELECT?
questions.why: A selection table is used with IN. It handles single values, ranges, patterns and exclusions at once.

questions.prompt: Which event is the standard place to validate selection screen input and show an error?
questions.why: AT SELECTION-SCREEN (or ON field) runs after input, so an error message there keeps the user on the screen.

questions.prompt: Which class gives the quickest way to show an internal table as an ALV grid in modern ABAP?
questions.why: cl_salv_table=>factory( ... ) followed by display( ) shows the table as an ALV with sorting and filtering built in.

questions.prompt: An ABAP class consists of which two parts?
questions.why: CLASS ... DEFINITION declares components; CLASS ... IMPLEMENTATION contains the method code.

questions.prompt: Which statement hard-codes a stop at that line in the debugger?
questions.why: BREAK-POINT stops execution in the debugger. Use it only while developing and remove it before transport. A session breakpoint in the editor margin is cleaner.

questions.prompt: An attribute declared in the PRIVATE SECTION can be accessed from:
questions.why: Private components are visible only within the class. Protected adds subclasses; public is visible to everyone.

questions.prompt: Which exception class is raised by a division by zero at runtime and can be caught with TRY ... CATCH?
questions.why: CX_SY_ZERODIVIDE is raised by the runtime and is catchable, so you can handle the error instead of a short dump.

questions.prompt: Which message type deliberately ends the program with a short dump?
questions.why: Type X raises the runtime error MESSAGE_TYPE_X. Type A ends the transaction with an abend message; S, I and E are normal messages.
